changes: Names stripped of the brahmin suffix bhaṭṭa: p1 'Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa' → 'Rāmeśvara', p2 'Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa' → 'Nārāyaṇa'; bhaṭṭa stays in titles.

p3: the scribe's name is in the cataloguer's crux (†…†) and may not be a name at all. It could be a garbled place or descriptive word before 'brāhmaṇena'. The string is kept as written, with low confidence and a note.

Date: the colophon gives two day-dates that don't agree: 'miti (vaiiśapya) vadī 10' (possibly Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 10?) and 'bhādrapada śuklā tṛtīyā ravau'. The second is kept as the main date and the conflict is now in notes.
Notes extended: the catalogue's 'ŚS 1848' doesn't match 'saṃvat 1885'. 1848 could be a misreading or a digit swap. In this context saṃvat with miti/vadī most likely means VS, so 1828 CE.

date.as_written: saṃvat 1885 miti (vaiiśapya) vadī (!) 10 saṃmaye (!) bhādrapada || śuklā tṛtīyā ravau

notes: 1) Date: the catalogue gives 'ŚS 1848', but the colophon reads 'saṃvat 1885'. 1848 may be a misreading or a digit swap. The era is not named. In this context saṃvat with miti/vadī most likely means VS 1885, about 1828 CE. If it were ŚS 1885, the date would be 1963 CE, which is unlikely. 2) The colophon has two day-dates that don't agree: 'miti (vaiiśapya) vadī 10' (perhaps Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 10) and 'bhādrapada śuklā tṛtīyā ravau'. The Bhādrapada date is recorded here. 3) Scribe: the cataloguer marks the text before 'brāhmaṇena' as corrupt (†yapurvehinaṇepīnāpya†). It may not be a personal name. It could, for example, contain a garbled place or ethnic word (…nepālīya?). The only certain point is that the scribe was a brāhmaṇa. 4) Nārāyaṇa, son of Rāmeśvara, wrote the Prākṛta commentary on the Śākuntala; he is not connected with this copy.
